name: Nambikuára, Southern
confidence_why: Kroeker 2001 and the two modern phonology dissertations, Mendes Costa 2020 on Nambikwara do Campo and Marques 2022 on Sararé, all put main stress on the root rather than on a fixed word-edge syllable and differ only on whether the stressed syllable inside the root is contrastive (Kroeker) or predictable from syllable weight with a rightmost default (Mendes Costa, Marques), while the only final-stress claim is StressTyp2's entry taken from a passage of Price 1976 that StressTyp2's own note calls unreliable.
catalog_quote: O acento de intensidade é fonêmico. A raiz recebe sempre o acento principal. Este não é marcado na ortografia por serem poucos os casos quando um falante nativo não iria saber onde termina a raiz e começa o sistema de sufixos.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog (StressTyp2) records fixed final stress (final stress). Kroeker 2001 places primary stress on the root, which in this suffixing language is at or near the beginning of the word, not on the last syllable; the language is also three-tone. Note the listed open_url (WALS refdb record 1973) is the wrong item (Lambton 1974, Persian Grammar); the DOI landing is behind an automated-access block; the copy read is the archive.org item 087-nambikuara (full scanned text; both PDF downloads truncated by archive.org stalls).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the root of the word (roots come first in this suffixing polysynthetic language, so stress sits on the root syllable near the left edge and never migrates to the suffix string, e.g. 'Kain-na-la 'it is big', A'luu-na-la 'it is long'); Kroeker calls stress phonemic because the root/suffix boundary is not always recoverable. Every syllable also carries one of three phonemic tones (falling, rising, low level) independent of stress; length is predictable from stress (the stressed syllable is longer).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; only 'primary stress' on the root is mentioned. Emphatic extra length on the stressed syllable (p. 82) is the only other prominence device described.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for placement; the morphophonemic rules (p. 84) treat post-stressed vowel deletion and consonant insertion relative to the stressed root syllable, with one lexical exception to vowel deletion (ex. 431).
new_statements.identity_note: Kroeker 2001 describes Nambikuara as a single language with mutually intelligible band dialects (Guaporé valley bands hahãintesu, alantesu, waikisu, wasusu, katitaulhu; Juruena/Parecis-plateau bands nesu, siwaisu, kithaulhu, saxwentesu, halotesu, wakalitesu), based on fieldwork since 1961 with speakers from several bands; this is the Southern Nambikwara (Nambikwara do Campo / do Sul) complex, matching sout2994. Kroeker 1982 (not opened) is tagged ISO nab, Southern Nambikuára, by the MPG record.

new_statements.translation: Intensity stress shows itself on the tonic syllable with more force than on the others. In the following examples it is marked by ' before the tonic syllable. In nouns, the last syllable of the root is the most intense: ka³la³ka³'la²su² 'chicken'. Generally, the intensity falls on the last syllable of the verb root: Sa²'so¹te³ra¹wa² 'I am going to fetch (get) it'. [preceded by:] In Nambikuara every syllable must be marked for tone. There are three tones ... Tone 1 falling, Tone 2 rising, Tone 3 low level.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (acento de intensidade) falls on the final syllable of the root: categorically so in nouns ('a última sílaba da raiz é mais intensa'), and 'generally' so in verbs (last syllable of the verb root), with the suffix string unstressed; stress is marked with an apostrophe only in the pronunciation key and in morphophonemic rules 9-11, not in the practical orthography. Tone is a separate system: three tones (falling, rising, low) marked on every syllable by superscript numerals. Syllables may additionally be lengthened (vowel or glottal) for emphasis ('duração enfática').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress (the pedagogical sketch marks only one stress per word; for secondary stress see Menno Kroeker 2001/2003 §25.4/§24.4 already held by the project).
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: 'Geralmente' (generally) the stress is on the last root syllable, so exceptions are implied but not listed. Morphophonemic rule 9 (p. 102): vowel contraction across a morpheme boundary applies only when the stress falls on the preceding morpheme and never in pretonic position (exception sa³in¹ -> san¹); rule 10: a transitional y/w/n is inserted between vowels of two morphemes when only one of them is stressed (æ³'e³te³ra¹wa² -> æ³'ye³te³ra¹wa², 'intensidade marcada por apóstrofo'); rule 11: the last stressed vowel of a word gains n before a following syllable-initial d.
new_statements.identity_note: Southern Nambikuára (nab) as spoken in the villages SIL worked in (Kroekers' fieldwork, cerrado/'Campo' groups and others; the sketch notes dialect differences only for the glottal consonants: 'o glotal está desaparecendo nas aldeias no cerrado'). Pedagogical grammar ('apostila') with a pronunciation key; it refers the compiler to Menno H. Kroeker 2003 Gramática descritiva for depth.

readall_conflicts: The catalog's StressTyp2 record gives fixed final stress, but the one source opened, Kroeker 2001 (p. 81), states that "the root always receives the primary stress" and that stress is phonemic, with three phonemic tones on every syllable; in this suffixing language the root is word-initial, so the catalog's final-stress reading is not supported by Kroeker. For context only (not in this work list): the Portuguese theses already held by the project from the compilation of 9/16 (Mendes Costa 2020, §4.1.3 "Atribuição do acento à raiz"; Marques 2022 on Sararé) also describe root stress, so the disagreement is between StressTyp2 and the descriptive literature, not among the descriptions. Kroeker 1982 could not be opened.

audit.recode_to: From 'lexical' to root-domain quantity-sensitive stress, right-edge default: primary stress always on the root; within the root stress the heavy syllable (branching rhyme: (C)VC / (C)V+glide), and if all root syllables are heavy or all light, the rightmost root syllable; affixes carry lexically marked stress that surfaces only as secondary; root-final /i/ extrametrical (Mendes Costa 2020:243-244, 249-251, 311-312; Marques 2022 for Sararé concurs). Domain should be ROOT/STEM, not word. The retirement of StressTyp2's all-final row stands (word-level position is morphology-driven, not count-based), but 'lexical / learned word by word' misdescribes a system the phonology of record calls 'previsível em raízes'.

sources.quote: Resumo: 'A posição do acento é previsível para palavras de conteúdo lexical com base nos parâmetros do peso da sílaba, da categoria lexical e da posição da sílaba dentro da raiz lexical. Ao contrário disso, os morfemas gramaticais devem ser marcados lexicamente por serem portadores de acento. O acento nos morfemas gramaticais sempre surge como secundário no nível da palavra fonológica.' (Sararé variety of Southern Nambikwara, which Glottolog files under sout2994.)
sources.locator: Resumo (p.~8) and ch.4 'Fonologia suprassegmental: acento e tom', pp.211-272
